newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Greenfields says agrees to 10-yr Enron deal.
newsitem.headline: Greenfields says agrees to 10-yr Enron deal.

text.p: Greenfields Coal Co Ltd said on Wednesday it has signed a letter of intent to supply 10 year coal fines offtake agreements with U.S utility Enron Capital and Trade.
Greenfields said it estimated revenue from the agreement would range from US$5.0 million to potentially over US$15 million for each of the 10 years.

Greenfields company secretary Peter Matthews said the take or pay agreement was for the supply of 720,000 tonnes of coal, including 480,000 tonnes of coal fines which Enron would use for synthetic fuel production.
The deal was due to be completed in mid-August.
Greenfields said it believed the agreement would provide the necessary revenues and profits to consolidate and expands its business in the United States.
Greenfields is developing the Alpheus coal reclamation plant in West Virginia and directors are currently negotiating funding to complete the third stage of the plant, Matthews said.
The finalising of the Enron agreement, which included a substantial prepayment provision, would enable the company to seek a mix of equity and debt funding, he added.
Greenfields is currently the subject of an unwelcome share-swap takeover offer from Canada's Mineral Resources Corp (MRC).
